checks: Seven recorded stages render; opening an approved Relay makes no commit or deployment call.
The project deployment command can be configured before committing; saving it performs neither delivery action.
The commit preview shows checkout, changed files and message; a separate explicit action sends the preview token and edited message.
Saving a project command does not run it; deployment shows the exact command and revision, starts explicitly, and remains cancellable.
Failure evidence and an explicit retry remain visible; completion is described as command execution with a recorded result.
Older relays keep five stages until explicitly extended, and a clean checkout offers a distinct existing-commit action.
A failed refresh disables delivery mutations; seven stages and the commit preview fit a narrow viewport.
Commit recovery reopens verification and review through one explicit request, keeps earlier evidence, and launches no agent.
New relays include explicit delivery stages by default; the composer can deliberately keep a review-only workflow.
